# Cogent Security Raises $42M Series A

Six months after launch, Cogent raises $42M led by Bain Capital Ventures to scale the first AI taskforce for vulnerability management.

Feb 18, 2026, 2 min read, Vineet Edupuganti, Co-Founder and CEO

Six months ago, we launched Cogent with a simple thesis: the hardest part of vulnerability management isn't finding the problems. It's fixing them.

Today, I'm excited to share that we've raised $42 million in Series A funding led by Bain Capital Ventures, with continued support from Greylock Partners and Definition. Founders and executives from OpenAI, Abnormal Security, and Datadog also invested personally. This brings our total funding to $53 million.

I'm especially proud to welcome [Enrique Salem](https://www.linkedin.com/in/enriquesalem/) to our Board of Directors. Enrique helped build and scale some of the defining security companies of the last two decades, including Symantec, Rubrik, and Netskope. He knows what it takes to turn a fast-growing security company into a lasting one, and we're lucky to have him.

## Why We're Here

The vulnerability management crisis has gotten worse since we launched. Over 48,000 new CVEs were published in the past year alone, 162 percent more than five years ago. And the window between a vulnerability being disclosed and an attacker exploiting it has collapsed, in part because attackers now use AI to move faster than ever.

Most security teams already have tools that find these issues. That's not the bottleneck. The bottleneck is everything after discovery: figuring out who owns the affected system, understanding why this specific vulnerability matters in this specific environment, getting the right fix in front of the right engineer, and confirming it actually got done. That work is still manual. It still involves chasing people through Slack threads and outdated spreadsheets. And it still takes days or weeks while attackers move in minutes.

Security teams don't have a visibility problem. They have an execution problem. That's the gap we built Cogent to close.

## What Cogent Does

Our AI agents handle the full lifecycle of vulnerability remediation. They investigate findings in the context of your actual environment, determine who owns what, assess real-world risk, generate remediation steps, and track fixes through to verified completion. Every action is traceable and auditable. Everything runs through configurable approval gates. Organizations deploy autonomous agents without giving up control.

Customers using Cogent have reduced their exposure windows for critical risks by an average of 97 percent. We're already working with dozens of Fortune 1000 companies and marquee brands across financial services, higher education, retail, and more.

## The Team

What I'm most proud of is the team we've assembled.

Our co-founders lived this problem firsthand. Geng and I came from Abnormal Security, where we helped scale the company from a small startup to a multibillion-dollar business. Thanos led infrastructure at Coinbase, where he ran large-scale vulnerability remediation programs. We've fused security product leaders from Abnormal, Zscaler, and Wiz with world-class AI and software talent from DeepMind, Coinbase, Databricks, Tesla, and Stripe. Our team includes AI researchers who helped develop the transformer architectures behind ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

It's a group of operators who have built category leaders and want to do it again.

## What's Next

This round of funding lets us double down on our core data and AI platforms, scale our go-to-market efforts, and hire exceptional builders. The future of cybersecurity will be agentic, and we're just getting started.

If you want to see what Cogent can do for your security program, [see the product](https://www.cogent.com/book-demo) for yourself. And if you're excited by the idea of building agentic AI from the ground up while making the digital world safer for everyone, we're hiring across R&D and GTM.

# Introducing Cogent Security

Cogent exits stealth with $11M in funding and a thesis: the hardest part of vulnerability management is everything after the scan.

Jul 14, 2025, 4 min read, Vineet Edupuganti, Co-Founder and CEO

## The First AI Taskforce for Vulnerability Management

Cogent Security is redefining how enterprises stay ahead of today’s relentless wave of vulnerabilities and exploits. We’re slashing remediation times, eliminating manual effort, and delivering real business impact, already protecting millions of assets across the Fortune 500 and beyond.

Today, we’re thrilled to launch out of stealth with $11 million in funding and the backing of world-class investors and advisors across security, enterprise software, and AI.

## Vulnerability Management Is at a Breaking Point

For decades, identifying and fixing vulnerabilities has been a cornerstone of enterprise cybersecurity. But in today’s rapidly evolving threat landscape, that cornerstone is cracking:

- Nearly 45,000 CVEs were published this year alone, 4x more than a decade ago¹
- Vulnerability exploitation is now the fastest growing cause of breaches globally per Verizon DBIR²
- Threat actors are moving faster than ever, cutting time-to-exploit in half thanks to generative AI³

Reinforcing these trends, high-profile incidents like Log4Shell have inflicted billions in damages, requiring multi-year remediation efforts. Meanwhile, most organizations are still relying on manual workflows, tribal knowledge, and endless back and forth between Security, Engineering, and IT.

Vulnerability management is no longer just inefficient, it’s unsustainable.

## A New Paradigm for VM: AI-Powered, Human-Level Judgment at Scale

Our founding team understands these challenges intimately. Over the past decade, we’ve been on the front lines, tackling critical vulnerabilities in high-stakes security environments at organizations like Coinbase, Blackstone, and Abnormal AI. Through this process, we experienced the constant struggle between balancing risk mitigation and business continuity, and navigating slow, siloed, and manual workflows.

This lived experience is why we built Cogent’s AI Taskforce, the first-ever fleet of AI agents purpose-built for end-to-end vulnerability remediation.

Unlike legacy tools that toss findings over the wall, our AI agents reason like human experts. They deeply understand your organization, collaborate as a virtual team, and drive actions all the way through resolution.

## Here’s how it works:

### 1. Understands Your Environment

Cogent's AI Taskforce continuously mines structured and unstructured data to build live, contextual models of your assets and risk surface.

### 2. Prioritizes What Matters

Modeled after real-world roles like VM Analysts and Infrastructure Engineers, our AI agents collaborate to:

- Derive ground truth context about assets and vulnerabilities
- Pinpoint top risks in real-time
- Generate personalized remediation strategies to map out who should do what by when

### 3. Drives to Resolution

Cogent's AI agents apply fixes directly or autonomously engage with downstream teams through the right channels. They operate with a nuanced understanding of business constraints like uptime or revenue risk, eliminating the need for constant intervention by Security.

All of this happens in seconds, at massive scale, powered by thousands of signals flowing through the Cogent AI Fabric.

## Production Grade AI, With Clear ROI

This isn't just theoretical. Cogent is already protecting leading global organizations, from public financial institutions to top-tier universities and Fortune 500 leaders.

The results from these engagements have been staggering: increases in remediation throughput, large declines in mean time to remediate, and a substantial reduction in VM Analyst time spent on vulnerability triage and remediation workstreams.

“Cogent handles the most labor-intensive parts of vulnerability management. That means Security, Engineering, and IT teams get hundreds of hours back each week. At scale, that’s millions of dollars in productivity gains and measurable improvements in risk posture for a large organization.”

— Lucas Moody, CISO @ Alteryx

## Building the Best Team in Cyber

The problem we are tackling is difficult and mission-critical. Cogent was born from the belief that modern security problems demand a new approach, and a world-class team to build it.

- Our founders previously helped scale Abnormal AI from a small startup to a $5B company, delivering cutting-edge behavioral AI solutions loved by thousands of security teams.
- Our technology is developed by the top software and AI engineers in Silicon Valley, who have built platforms, infrastructure, and domain-specific AI Agents at mega scale at companies such as Coinbase, Tesla, and Google Research.
- This technical prowess is amplified by the domain and workflow expertise of our in-house vulnerability management team, which has decades of combined experience building and managing VM programs for marquee clients at MSSPs like Guidepoint Security and Optiv and industry pioneers like Kenna and ZScaler.

We are incredibly grateful to be on this journey with a trusted set of investors and advisors. Our Seed round was led by Greylock Partners (backers of Palo Alto Networks, Okta, Wiz, and others). Our advisors and angel investors include former founders and executives from Tenable and Crowdstrike, ex-CISOs, and leading minds from companies like OpenAI.

## The Road Ahead

Our progress to this point has been faster than we could have envisioned, and we have an exciting roadmap ahead.

If you are interested in supercharging your VM program, get started for free. And if you're excited by the idea of building Agentic AI from the ground up while making the digital world safer for everyone, we are hiring for all roles across R&D and GTM.

# Cogent Security Gets $42M to Boost AI Vulnerability Defense

Series A Led by Bain Capital Ventures Targets Autonomous Remediation Platform Michael Novinson(MichaelNovinson) • February 19, 2026 https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/cogent-security-gets-42m-to-boost-ai-vulnerability-defense-a-30804#disqus_thread

Vineet Edupuganti, co-founder and CEO, Cogent Security (Image: Cogent Security)

An early-stage startup led by a former Abnormal AI division head raised $42 million to better ingest and reconcile massive volumes of enterprise security data.

See Also: How Skilled Attackers Weaponize AI Faster

The Bain Capital Ventures-led Series A funding will enable San Francisco-based Cogent Security to scale its architecture to handle increasingly complex enterprise environments, reconcile conflicting data sources and improve artificial intelligence reliability in security use cases, said CEO Vineet Edupuganti. The money will address the data and context layer, the AI agent development platform, and the modeling and research layer.

"We spent the last year really building conviction in the space that we're working in, setting the right foundation in terms of our team, product, early customers," Edupuganti told Information Security Media Group. "With this round, we wanted to pour our fuel on the fire and double down on the things that are working, and we have plans to scale very aggressively."

Cogent, founded in 2024, employs 37 people and has raised $53 million, having emerged from stealth in July 2025 with $11 million in seed funding from Greylock Partners. The company has been led since inception by Edupuganti, who spent four years at Abnormal, culminating in an 11-month role leading the company's 30-peson multi-product platform division (see: Fighting AI Threats With Behavior-Based Awareness Training).

### Why Maintaining a Fleet of AI Agents Is Such a Heavy Lift

Edupuganti said the capital is earmarked for significantly increasing headcount. The money will help Cogent to bring its defensive AI capabilities to more enterprises facing increasingly AI-enabled threats, Edupuganti said.

"We're going to triple the team over the course of this year, invest very heavily into R&D, and at the same time, scale our go-to-market team so we can expand our impact to more customers," Edupuganti said.

Enterprise security environments are extraordinarily fragmented and data-heavy, and Edupuganti said companies rely on EDR platforms, vulnerability scanners and CMDB systems that generate overlapping, and sometimes conflicting, information. Determining the authoritative source of truth becomes very complex as the number of integrations grows from two or three to a dozen or more, Edupuganti said.

"What we've proven is that we can take some core datasets and organize those datasets and help to drive action," Edupuganti said. "One area that is going to be critical as we mature is scaling to the biggest environments. One thing that's really critical is architecturally setting ourselves up to achieve high performance at scale. Because generally, performance degrades at scale."

Nearly every major function at Cogent - from integration management to vulnerability prioritization and remediation planning - is powered by agents, but Edupuganti said building, testing, evaluating and maintaining dozens of agents requires significant engineering effort. Cogent is building a development process that reduces both the upfront cost of spinning up new agents and the variable cost of maintaining them.

"We have AI agents that power pretty much every component of the platform," Edupuganti said. "That's things like our integrations, platform reporting, use cases, gathering asset context, prioritizing vulnerabilities, building remediation plans. Basically everything is meant to be an agent. That's also why we're able to solve some of the challenges we're able to solve for that couldn't be tackled previously."

### Why Foundational Models Fall Short in Specialized Domains

Foundational models excel in code generation and general text transformation but fall short in highly specialized domains like vulnerability management since these workflows often involve contextual nuances and environmental dependencies not well represented in public training data. Achieving the necessary reliability requires post-training refinement, domain-specific data curation and research.

"In terms of getting into the nitty gritty details of what will happen when you try to patch some system, it can be tough," Edupuganti said. "Because for some of these patterns of context and environmental details, it's not like there's some knowledge base that necessarily pre-exists."

Autonomous remediation will help organizations reduce risk without relying entirely on human-driven processes, cutting down attack paths before adversaries can exploit them, Edupuganti said. Cogent's strategy is to first deliver operational uplift through automation of labor-intensive triage and analysis tasks, then to gradually guide customers toward greater autonomy.

"If you can know, 'Here's the risk performance of an organization and here's a safe way of mitigating the risk,' that's the ultimate unlock for auto remediation," Edupuganti said. "Can you actually get to a world in which you don't have to rely on humans and you can cut down attack paths before attackers can break in? That is the holy grail that we're pioneering towards."

Customer count is a leading indicator of market validation and expanded impact, but Edupuganti said growth must be matched by measurable product performance. Key product metrics include remediation accuracy, reduction in mean time to remediate and operational efficiency gains for security teams. He said Cogent customers should see significant MTTR reductions and reduced manual workload.

"What is the accuracy of our remediation recommendations? How much are we impacting MTTR for customers?" Edupuganti said. "The mean time to remediate that should be going down and to the right by significant margins as you use Cogent. When you start using Cogent, your security team, your role management team should get way more efficient."

Cogent Security Raises $42M Series A to Arm Security Teams With Autonomous AI Agents Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation

Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Greylock, Cogent builds agentic systems to fight off escalating AI threats

SAN FRANCISCO, Feb. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cogent Security today announced $42 million in Series A funding led by Bain Capital Ventures, with participation from existing investor Greylock Partners and Definition. Founders and executives from OpenAI, Abnormal Security, and Datadog invested personally. The financing brings Cogent's total funding to $53 million, just six months after the company's official launch.

Why Attackers Are Winning

In 2025, over 48,000 new software vulnerabilities known as CVEs were published. That's 162 percent higher than five years ago. Every enterprise software system has them, and new ones appear constantly as code changes and new threats emerge. Meanwhile, the time needed for hackers to figure out how to exploit new vulnerabilities has collapsed.

Attackers and security teams now operate at completely different speeds. Hackers using AI begin probing enterprises for vulnerabilities minutes after they're first published. Fixing one on the defensive side still takes days or weeks. Security teams hunt down system owners through outdated directories and Slack threads. Developers field tickets without knowing which systems are affected or why this particular issue matters more than the hundreds of others in their queue.

Security backlogs grow faster than teams can clear them. Banks, hospitals, retailers, manufacturers, energy companies—they all face the same problem.

Finding vulnerabilities isn't the hard part. Modern scanning tools handle discovery. The hard part is everything after: figuring out who owns what, understanding real-world risk, coordinating fixes across teams, proving the work was completed. It's slow. It's manual. And the threats now move at machine speed.

"Security teams are drowning in coordination work: chasing down system owners, writing tickets, proving fixes happened. We built AI agents that handle that work end-to-end, so security teams can finally keep pace with attackers," said Vineet Edupuganti, CEO and co-founder of Cogent.

Cogent Security: AI Agents That Automate Remediation

Traditional security tools stop at detection, surfacing findings and leaving humans to handle the rest. Cogent's AI agents investigate vulnerabilities, determine system ownership, assess real-world risk based on the environment, and generate remediation steps ready for engineers to implement. The agents then track fixes through to verified completion. Customers using Cogent have reduced exposure windows for critical risks by an average of 97 percent.

Cogent is built for enterprise governance. Every agent action is traceable and reproducible. The platform integrates directly into existing security and engineering workflows and operates under configurable approval gates and policy enforcement. Organizations can deploy autonomous AI agents without sacrificing control, auditability, or human oversight.

CSC is the leading AI-driven consolidator in commerce, having acquired Backcountry.com and four other brands in the past year alone. "Given the pace of our M&A activity, Cogent is central to our cybersecurity strategy—autonomously managing risk without slowing us down so we can stay focused on deploying AI," said Justin Yoshimura, CEO of CSC Generation. # The Five Laws of Cogent: Product Principles for Security Teams That Expect More

Most security tools force a choice between power and usability. Five product principles that explain why Cogent refuses the tradeoff.

Jul 10, 2025, 2 min read, Vineet Edupuganti, Co-Founder and CEO

Most security tools force you to choose between capability and usability. They’re either powerful but hard to operate, or simple but incomplete. At Cogent, we believe that’s a false tradeoff, and we’re proving it with a new kind of product, designed from first principles to actually solve vulnerability management end-to-end.

We’re not guessing what modern security teams need. At Abnormal AI, we built advanced detection systems used by thousands of enterprises. We saw how clunky tools, manual processes, and poor collaboration held teams back. We also saw how intuitive, well-designed products accelerate adoption, improve outcomes, and make security a business enabler.

These experiences shaped the five core principles guiding everything we build at Cogent:

### 1. Simplicity

Cogent is designed to be easy to understand and operate. Security leaders don’t have time for complexity, and engineers shouldn't require a steep learning curve to use a product. From the UI to workflow automation, everything is built for clarity, so teams can quickly see top risks, the work that is getting done, and top-level metrics with a certification-free, consumer-grade experience.

### 2. Completeness

Security teams shouldn't have to glue together multiple tools to manage vulnerabilities. Cogent is built to cover the entire vulnerability lifecycle between scan and patch across broad areas of your attack surface. No stitching together partial solutions or maintaining custom scripts. Just one system that works out of the box.

### 3. Autonomy

Cogent's AI agents don't just make suggestions, they take action. They apply fixes, engage the right teams, and do so with full awareness of business constraints like uptime or ownership. Security teams get leverage without needing to micromanage every individual workflow.

### 4. Self-Serve

Cogent is designed to be usable without relying on support or services. Most configurations and integrations can be done directly by users. If something isn’t self-serve, we fix it in the product to ensure a smooth, transparent experience.

### 5. Product-First

When customers run into friction, we don't write an Ops playbook, we ship product. Every pain point is treated as a roadmap opportunity, not a support ticket. That mindset helped us build a category leading solution at Abnormal, and it’s how we’re building Cogent: through fast iteration, customer feedback, and constant improvement.

## Why It Matters for Security Leaders

Security teams are under constant pressure to do more with less. They need to reduce risk, cut noise, and avoid burn out across both their team and cross-functional partners.

Cogent was built to give you leverage. Our foundational product principles ensure that the product drives results with minimal overhead, fewer surprises, and better alignment with how your organization actually works.

# Figma Never: Code Is the New Canvas

AI code generation killed the Figma-first workflow. Cogent's design team now ships directly in code, and the results are faster and better.

Feb 26, 2026, 2 min read, Hyun Kim, Designer

At the end of October, I published an article called Figma Last.

The thesis was simple. Stop starting in Figma. Validate earlier. Build sooner. Figma should not be first. It should be last.

A few months later, that workflow has become unrecognizable.

That is how fast this is moving.

Back then, I was reacting to Figma First. The default loop. Open a blank canvas. Design static mocks. Annotate edge cases. Hand off. Wait for engineering to reinterpret your intent.

Figma Last moved validation closer to execution.

Figma Never removes the abstraction entirely.

Today the work starts in the terminal.

Before a single UI component exists, I open Claude Code in plan mode through the CLI. I create a design PRD. Not a bloated template. A sharp articulation of the problem, flows, constraints, tradeoffs, and edge cases. I use it as a thought partner. I challenge assumptions and simplify complexity before it hardens into UI.

Then we build.

I pair Claude Code with Agentation (annotation tool) to structure intent and generate components aligned to our system. I scaffold. I iterate. I push to a dev environment.

Within hours, there is something real. Engineers wire the backend. Data flows. States behave. Edge cases surface immediately. We refine inside the product, not in a picture of it.

This shift has dramatically increased my productivity. But the more meaningful change is how I see my role. I think less in terms of product designer or design engineer and more in terms of a builder.

Because that is what this actually is.

I can shape high level flows in the morning and tune micro animations in a tab icon in the afternoon. I can adjust motion curves directly in the component. I can test hierarchy against live data instead of placeholder states. The control is immediate.

For the first time in my career, something feels unlocked. Architects historically drafted buildings they never physically constructed. As software builders, we now conceive and build in the same medium.

The system itself has changed too.

I injected my design taste into Claude as a skill. My preferences around spacing, density, hierarchy, motion, and interaction patterns. My bias toward clarity. My intolerance for noise. It understands how I think about UI/UX.

My design system is no longer a static document. It is encoded behavior.

I built a lightweight internal Storybook that acts as a living source of truth. It is visually browsable but fully manipulable in code. Tokens, variants, motion primitives all live where they execute. When new features are generated, they align automatically because the system is embedded upstream.

This is the real progression.

**Figma First **was static ownership.
Figma Last moved validation closer to engineering.
Figma Never removes the layer entirely.

Code is now the shared material. PMs express intent in text. Designers shape experience structurally. Engineers enforce systems integrity. We meet at execution.

And once you work this way, going back to Figma feels primitive. It feels like stepping out of a living system and into a drawing of one.

The shift happened fast.

Figma First was default.
Figma Last felt radical in October.
Now Figma Never feels inevitable.

We do not design pictures of software.

We design software.

If you are still spending most of your time in Figma pushing pixels, managing pristine component files, writing spec-heavy PRDs disconnected from execution, annotating hover states that only exist in comment bubbles, and presenting static mocks that simulate behavior instead of proving it, you’re optimizing for irrelevance.

Vineet Edupuganti, co-founder and CEO, Cogent Security (Image: Cogent Security)

An early-stage startup led by a former Abnormal AI division head raised $42 million to better ingest and reconcile massive volumes of enterprise security data.

See Also: Why an AI Harness May Matter More Than the Latest Model

The Bain Capital Ventures-led Series A funding will enable San Francisco-based Cogent Security to scale its architecture to handle increasingly complex enterprise environments, reconcile conflicting data sources and improve artificial intelligence reliability in security use cases, said CEO Vineet Edupuganti. The money will address the data and context layer, the AI agent development platform, and the modeling and research layer.

"We spent the last year really building conviction in the space that we're working in, setting the right foundation in terms of our team, product, early customers," Edupuganti told Information Security Media Group. "With this round, we wanted to pour our fuel on the fire and double down on the things that are working, and we have plans to scale very aggressively."

Cogent, founded in 2024, employs 37 people and has raised $53 million, having emerged from stealth in July 2025 with $11 million in seed funding from Greylock Partners. The company has been led since inception by Edupuganti, who spent four years at Abnormal, culminating in an 11-month role leading the company's 30-peson multi-product platform division (see: Fighting AI Threats With Behavior-Based Awareness Training).

### Why Maintaining a Fleet of AI Agents Is Such a Heavy Lift

Edupuganti said the capital is earmarked for significantly increasing headcount. The money will help Cogent to bring its defensive AI capabilities to more enterprises facing increasingly AI-enabled threats, Edupuganti said.

"We're going to triple the team over the course of this year, invest very heavily into R&D, and at the same time, scale our go-to-market team so we can expand our impact to more customers," Edupuganti said.

Enterprise security environments are extraordinarily fragmented and data-heavy, and Edupuganti said companies rely on EDR platforms, vulnerability scanners and CMDB systems that generate overlapping, and sometimes conflicting, information. Determining the authoritative source of truth becomes very complex as the number of integrations grows from two or three to a dozen or more, Edupuganti said.

"What we've proven is that we can take some core datasets and organize those datasets and help to drive action," Edupuganti said. "One area that is going to be critical as we mature is scaling to the biggest environments. One thing that's really critical is architecturally setting ourselves up to achieve high performance at scale. Because generally, performance degrades at scale."

Nearly every major function at Cogent - from integration management to vulnerability prioritization and remediation planning - is powered by agents, but Edupuganti said building, testing, evaluating and maintaining dozens of agents requires significant engineering effort. Cogent is building a development process that reduces both the upfront cost of spinning up new agents and the variable cost of maintaining them.

"We have AI agents that power pretty much every component of the platform," Edupuganti said. "That's things like our integrations, platform reporting, use cases, gathering asset context, prioritizing vulnerabilities, building remediation plans. Basically everything is meant to be an agent. That's also why we're able to solve some of the challenges we're able to solve for that couldn't be tackled previously."

### Why Foundational Models Fall Short in Specialized Domains

Foundational models excel in code generation and general text transformation but fall short in highly specialized domains like vulnerability management since these workflows often involve contextual nuances and environmental dependencies not well represented in public training data. Achieving the necessary reliability requires post-training refinement, domain-specific data curation and research.

"In terms of getting into the nitty gritty details of what will happen when you try to patch some system, it can be tough," Edupuganti said. "Because for some of these patterns of context and environmental details, it's not like there's some knowledge base that necessarily pre-exists."

Autonomous remediation will help organizations reduce risk without relying entirely on human-driven processes, cutting down attack paths before adversaries can exploit them, Edupuganti said. Cogent's strategy is to first deliver operational uplift through automation of labor-intensive triage and analysis tasks, then to gradually guide customers toward greater autonomy.

"If you can know, 'Here's the risk performance of an organization and here's a safe way of mitigating the risk,' that's the ultimate unlock for auto remediation," Edupuganti said.
